<content>
1: # SwapDesk
2: 
3: SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.
4: 
5: All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.
6: 
7: ## Repository layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: frontend/          Next.js dashboard — standalone client-side demo (no backend required)
11: src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
12: eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
13: tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
14: docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
15: hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
16: ```
17: 
18: ## The two halves
19: 
20: - **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
21: - **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It is a **self-contained client-side demo** powered by a mock store — it demos the SwapDesk experience without calling the live API. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## Backend
26: 
27: ### Features
28: 
29: - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
30: - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
31: - Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
32: - One active exchange per order item, across cases.
33: - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
34: - Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
35: - Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
36: - A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
37: - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).
38: 
39: ### Installation
40: 
41: Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
42: 
43: ```bash
44: git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
45: cd SwapDesk
46: uv sync
47: ```
48: 
49: ### Test
50: 
51: ```bash
52: uv run pytest -q
53: ```
54: 
55: The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.
56: 
57: ### Run the API
58: 
59: ```bash
60: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app
61: ```
62: 
63: Interactive docs at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always in sync). The demo database is `swapdesk.db` (override with `SWAPDESK_DB`); restarting reuses it, fixtures seed once.
64: 
65: | Method & route                 | What it does                                                              |
66: | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67: | `POST /v1/tickets`             | Submit a ticket and run it to a verified outcome (201)                    |
68: | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`       | Run natural-language input through the checkpointed LangGraph agent (201) |
69: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`           | Verified status, outcome, reply, run ids (404 unknown)                    |
70: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`  | Sanitized action/journal events (404 unknown)                             |
71: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue` | Continue with message/consent (404 unknown, 422 uncontinuable)            |
72: | `GET /v1/fixtures`             | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns                         |
73: | `POST /v1/demo/faults`         | Demo-only: arm one failure on an operation key                            |
74: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`       | Demo-only: disarm all failures                                            |
75: | `GET /v1/health`               | Liveness probe                                                            |
76: 
77: Outcomes (`arranged`, `clarification`, `denial`, `escalation`) are response data, not transport errors. Ticket creation routes return 201 with an `outcome`; case status reads return 200. Malformed requests return 422, unknown cases 404, an unconfigured agent 503, and an agent execution failure 502 with the case identity needed to retry.
78: 
79: `POST /v1/tickets` remains the deterministic demo path. Use `/v1/agent/tickets` for model-driven handling; it requires an agent provider configuration. Supply a stable `case_id` when a caller may need to retry after a gateway failure. Retry that request with the same case ID and `"resume": true` to continue from its SQLite checkpoint. The route accepts optional structured order fields as hints; the customer message remains the agent's primary input.
80: 
81: ```bash
82: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/tickets \
83:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
84:   -d '{"case_id":"CASE-CLIENT-123","message":"Exchange item ITEM-01 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
85: ```
86: 
87: ```bash
88: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/tickets \
89:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
90:   -d '{"order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
91: 
92: curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx
93: curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
94: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
95:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
96:   -d '{"consent_size":"42","order_id":"ORD-1005","order_item_id":"ITEM-06","size":"43"}'
97: ```
98: 
99: No authentication: this is a local mock. Execution runs synchronously per request, so status reads are never blocked.
100: 
101: ### Configuring the agent
102: 
103: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):
104: 
105: - `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
106: - `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
107: - `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
108: - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.
109: 
110: Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.
111: 
112: ### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio
113: 
114: Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
115: 
116: ```bash
117: uv run langgraph dev
118: ```
119: 
120: Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:
121: 
122: - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
123: - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.
124: 
125: Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
126: 
127: ## Frontend
128: 
129: A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.
130: 
131: ### Run it
132: 
133: ```bash
134: cd frontend
135: npm install
136: npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
137: ```
138: 
139: Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.
140: 
141: ### Pages and demo flow
142: 
143: | Route           | Page                | What it demos                                        |
144: | --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
145: | `/`             | Mission Control     | Agent metrics + live execution queue                 |
146: | `/inbox`        | Inbox               | Sample ticket stream                                 |
147: | `/inventory`    | Inventory           | Stock levels that react to simulations               |
148: | `/database`     | Database Schema     | Tables the agent reads/writes                        |
149: | `/integrations` | Integrations        | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
150: | `/settings`     | Agent Settings      | Autonomy/guardrail config UI                         |
151: | `/simulate`     | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue           |
152: | `/ticket/[id]`  | Ticket Execution    | Per-ticket action timeline                           |
153: 
154: The demo runs entirely on a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`). **Simulate Ticket** prepends a resolved ticket and decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock; **Customer Simulation** injects a ticket with an `Agent Processing` status; **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the initial state. Dashboard labels reflect the actual mock state — completion rate is computed from the queue, and cost shows "Demo Mode".
155: 
156: SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.
157: 
158: ## Evaluation and evidence
159: 
160: - `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
161: - `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
162: - `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
163: - `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
164: - `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.
165: 
166: ## Documentation
167: 
168: | Doc                                                                  | Purpose                                                                                         |
169: | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
170: | [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md)                           | Full build plan (spec, not evidence)                                                            |
171: | [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md)         | LangGraph Studio runbook with evidence                                                          |
172: | [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through                                                            |
173: | [`docs/business/`](docs/business/)                                   | Business plan (MD/PDF) and financial model (XLSX) — figures are assumptions, not observed facts |
174: | [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md)                                       | Slice-by-slice build log and conventions                                                        |
175: 
176: ## Contributing
177: 
178: - Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
179: - Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
180: - Record each slice in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
181: - Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.

1: """HTTP API for frontend teammates. One concern only: HTTP ↔ service.
2: 
3: Business outcomes (arranged/clarification/denial/escalation) are always
4: HTTP 200 with an `outcome` field: a denial is an answer, not an error.
5: HTTP errors mean transport problems only: 404 unknown case, 422 bad
6: request, 500 unexpected failure (generic message, never internals).
7: 
8: Execution is synchronous per request; the demo database makes status
9: reads available at any time. No authentication: this is a local mock,
10: and the docs say so. Demo-only failure controls live under /v1/demo
11: and never touch ordinary endpoints.
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: from pathlib import Path
17: from typing import Any
18: 
19: from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
20: from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
21: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
22: 
23: from . import service
24: from .agent.graph import ConfigurationError
25: from .operations import OperationError
26: 
27: FAULT_POINTS = {"transient", "deplete_stock", "crash", "timeout",
28:                 "release_fail"}
29: FAULT_STEPS = {"reserve", "return", "label", "finalize", "escalate",
30:                "cancel"}
31: 
32: 
33: class TicketIn(BaseModel):
34:     order_id: str
35:     order_item_id: str
36:     size: str = ""
37:     qty: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)
38:     message: str = ""
39:     consent_size: str | None = None
40:     case_id: str | None = None
41: 
42: 
43: class TicketOut(BaseModel):

1: # SwapDesk Frontend
2: 
3: The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.
4: 
5: Built as a self-contained Next.js app with **client-side demo state** — no backend is required to run or demo it.
6: 
7: ## Tech Stack
8: 
9: - **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
10: - **React 19** with Server & Client Components
11: - **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
12: - **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
13: - **lucide-react** icons
14: - **sonner** toasts
15: - Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)
16: 
17: ## Getting Started
18: 
19: ```bash
20: npm install      # install dependencies
21: npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
22: ```
23: 
24: Other scripts:
25: 
26: | Script          | Description                                    |
27: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
28: | `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
29: | `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
30: | `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |
31: 
32: ## Environment Variables
33: 
34: | Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
35: | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |
37: 
38: ## Project Structure
39: 
40: ```
41: app/
42: ├── layout.tsx              # Root layout, global <head> metadata, fonts, SwapDeskProvider, Toaster
43: ├── page.tsx                # Server entry → renders <MissionControl />
44: ├── mission-control.tsx     # "Mission Control" home (client) — metrics + live queue
45: ├── inbox/page.tsx          # Full ticket inbox (static demo data)
46: ├── inventory/              # Live stock + reservations (client; stock reacts to simulations)
47: │   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
48: │   └── page.tsx
49: ├── database/layout.tsx     # Schema view (metadata)
50: ├── integrations/           # Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify Inbox, Gorgias)
51: │   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
52: │   └── page.tsx
53: ├── settings/layout.tsx     # Agent autonomy/guardrail settings (metadata)
54: ├── simulate/page.tsx       # Customer Simulation — inject a ticket into the queue
55: ├── ticket/[id]/page.tsx    # Ticket execution detail (Suspense split; see below)
56: ├── robots.ts               # /robots.txt
57: ├── sitemap.ts              # /sitemap.xml
58: ├── opengraph-image.tsx     # Generated OG image (ImageResponse)
59: ├── twitter-image.tsx       # Re-exports from opengraph-image
60: └── globals.css             # Theme tokens + utilities (panel, glass, pulse-dot, num, rise)
61: 
62: src/
63: ├── components/
64: │   ├── AppShell.tsx                # Sidebar + top bar + mobile bottom nav, "Simulate Ticket" button
65: │   └── CustomerSimulationWidget.tsx
66: ├── lib/
67: │   ├── seo.ts                      # SITE_* constants + pageMetadata() helper
68: │   └── utils.ts                    # cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge)
69: └── store/
70:     └── swapdesk.tsx                # Global demo state + SwapDeskProvider
71: ```
72: 
73: ## Demo Flow
74: 
75: Everything is driven by a client-side store — no network calls.
76: 
77: 1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`), type a complaint, and submit.
78: 2. The store appends a ticket with status `Agent Processing` (`INTAKE` / `ROUTING` actions).
79: 3. It appears instantly in **Mission Control** and the **Inbox**, filterable by status.
80: 4. Open any ticket to inspect its execution timeline, actions, and SKU reservation.
81: 5. **Simulate Ticket** also decrements stock for `AJ4-MIL-43` (5 → 4) — visible on `/inventory`.
82: 6. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears tickets and restores stock.
83: 
84: ## State Management
85: 
86: `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:
87: 
88: ```ts
89: const { tickets, inventory, simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket } =
90:   useSwapDesk();
91: ```
92: 
93: - `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"`
94: - `simulateTicket(): Ticket` — prepends `TCK-9045+` resolved ticket, decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock.
95: - `submitCustomerTicket(message): Ticket` — prepends a `processing` ticket with your message.
96: - `resetMockData()` — wipes tickets, restores initial inventory.
97: - `getTicket(id)` — look up a single ticket.
98: 
99: ## Routes
100: 
101: | Route                 | Page                    | Type            | Notes                              |
102: | --------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
103: | `/`                   | Mission Control         | server + client | metrics + live queue, filter       |
104: | `/inbox`              | Inbox                   | server          | static ticket list                 |
105: | `/inventory`          | Inventory               | server layout + client page | stock reacts to simulations |
106: | `/database`           | Database Schema         | server          |                                    |
107: | `/integrations`       | Integrations            | server layout + client page | webhook toggle + URL copy  |
108: | `/settings`           | Agent Settings          | server          |                                    |
109: | `/simulate`           | Customer Simulation     | server          | `CustomerSimulationWidget`         |
110: | `/ticket/[id]`        | Ticket Execution        | client          | Partial Prerender (Suspense)       |
111: | `/robots.txt`         | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
112: | `/sitemap.xml`        | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
113: | `/opengraph-image`    | —                       | image route     | generated 1200×630 PNG             |
114: | `/twitter-image`      | —                       | image route     | re-export of opengraph-image       |
115: 
116: > **Turbopack dynamic route note:** `/ticket/[id]` must pre-render its HTML shell at build time. Client hooks that need URL data (`useParams`, `usePathname`) therefore live behind `<Suspense>` and out of the static shell. See `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`.
117: 
118: ## Design System
119: 
120: Theme tokens live in `app/globals.css` as CSS variables and Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings:
121: 
122: - Colors: `--card: #111113`, `--border: #222225`, `--color-success` (green), `--color-primary`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`, `--color-hairline`
123: - Type: `font-display` (`--font-bricolage`), `font-sans` (`--font-jakarta`), `font-mono` (`--font-geist-mono`)
124: - Utilities: `panel` (card), `glass` (frosted nav), `pulse-dot`, `num` (tabular numerals), `rise` (entry animation)
125: 
126: > **Guideline:** keep server-rendered pages static where possible and move interactivity into client components. Do not introduce a visual redesign — extend the existing token system.
127: 
128: ## SEO
129: 
130: Add full metadata to every segment:
131: 
132: - Root (`app/layout.tsx`): `metadataBase`, titles with `template: "%s · SwapDesk"`, description, keywords, `<viewport>` (themeColor), OpenGraph + Twitter cards, `robots`, `applicationName`, authors, category.
133: - Per page: use the `pageMetadata({ title, description, path })` helper from `src/lib/seo.ts` (marked `Export const metadata`).
134: - Images: `app/opengraph-image.tsx` generates a themed 1200×630 card with `ImageResponse`; `app/twitter-image.tsx` re-exports it.
135: - Crawling: `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` reflect the remaining routes.
136: 
137: Set the title without the site name suffix — the root template appends ` · SwapDesk`.
138: 
139: ## Deploy
140: 
141: Deploy on Vercel (or any Node host running `npm run build && npm run start`):
142: 
143: ```bash
144: npm run build
145: npm run start
146: ```
147: 
148: Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your production origin so canonical URLs, sitemap, and robots are correct.

(End of file - total 148 lines)

1: "use client";
2: 
3: import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
4: 
5: export type TicketStatus = "resolved" | "escalated" | "processing";
6: 
7: export type Ticket = {
8:   id: string;
9:   message: string;
10:   status: TicketStatus;
11:   statusLabel: string;
12:   actions: string[];
13:   time: string;
14:   sku: string;
15: };
16: 
17: export type InventoryItem = {
18:   sku: string;
19:   name: string;
20:   size: number;
21:   stock: number;
22:   res: number;
23:   wh: string;
24: };
25: 
26: export const MOCK_TICKET = {
27:   message: "Jordan 4 size 43 exchange",
28:   status: "resolved" as TicketStatus,
29:   statusLabel: "Resolved Autonomously",
30:   actions: ["RESERVE_STOCK", "CREATE_LABEL"],
31:   time: "Just now",
32:   sku: "AJ4-MIL-43",
33: };
34: 
35: const createInitialTickets = (): Ticket[] => [
36:   {
37:     id: "TCK-9042",
38:     message: "Jordan 4s are too tight, need size 43.",
39:     status: "resolved",
40:     statusLabel: "Resolved Autonomously",
41:     actions: ["RESERVE_STOCK", "CREATE_LABEL"],
42:     time: "Just now",
43:     sku: "AJ4-MIL-43",
44:   },
45:   {
46:     id: "TCK-9043",
47:     message: "I want a refund but I bought these 90 days ago.",
48:     status: "escalated",
49:     statusLabel: "Escalated to Human",
50:     actions: ["POLICY_DENY"],
51:     time: "2 min ago",
52:     sku: "SMB-OG-41",
53:   },
54:   {
55:     id: "TCK-9044",
56:     message: "Need a size 10 exchange.",
57:     status: "resolved",
58:     statusLabel: "Resolved (Recovered)",
59:     actions: ["API_TIMEOUT_RECOVERED"],
60:     time: "5 min ago",
61:     sku: "GK30-BLK-44",
62:   },
63: ];
64: 
65: const createInitialInventory = (): InventoryItem[] => [
66:   { sku: "AJ4-MIL-43", name: "Air Jordan 4 Military", size: 43, stock: 5, res: 1, wh: "WH-AMS-02" },
67:   { sku: "AJ4-MIL-42", name: "Air Jordan 4 Military", size: 42, stock: 3, res: 0, wh: "WH-AMS-02" },
68:   { sku: "SMB-OG-41", name: "Adidas Samba OG", size: 41, stock: 12, res: 2, wh: "WH-BER-01" },
69:   { sku: "NB550-GRY-39", name: "New Balance 550 Grey", size: 39, stock: 0, res: 0, wh: "WH-BER-01" },
70:   { sku: "GK30-BLK-44", name: "Asics Gel-Kayano 30", size: 44, stock: 5, res: 1, wh: "WH-AMS-02" },
71: ];
72: 
73: type SwapDeskContextValue = {
74:   tickets: Ticket[];
75:   inventory: InventoryItem[];
76:   simulateTicket: () => Ticket;
77:   submitCustomerTicket: (message: string) => Ticket;
78:   resetMockData: () => void;
79:   getTicket: (id: string) => Ticket | undefined;
80: };
81: 
82: const SwapDeskContext = createContext<SwapDeskContextValue | null>(null);
83: 
84: export function SwapDeskProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
85:   const [tickets, setTickets] = useState<Ticket[]>(createInitialTickets);
86:   const [inventory, setInventory] = useState<InventoryItem[]>(createInitialInventory);
87:   const seq = useRef(9045);
88: 
89:   const simulateTicket = useCallback(() => {
90:     const ticket: Ticket = { id: `TCK-${seq.current++}`, ...MOCK_TICKET };
91:     setTickets((prev) => [ticket, ...prev]);
92:     setInventory((prev) =>
93:       prev.map((item) =>
94:         item.sku === MOCK_TICKET.sku
95:           ? { ...item, stock: Math.max(0, item.stock - 1), res: item.res + 1 }
96:           : item,
97:       ),
98:     );
99:     return ticket;
100:   }, []);
101: 
102:   const submitCustomerTicket = useCallback((message: string) => {
103:     const text = message.trim() || "My Jordan 4s arrived but are too tight. I need to exchange for a size 43.";
104:     const ticket: Ticket = {
105:       id: `TCK-${seq.current++}`,
106:       message: text,
107:       status: "processing",
108:       statusLabel: "Agent Processing",
109:       actions: ["INTAKE", "ROUTING"],
110:       time: "Just now",
111:       sku: "AJ4-MIL-43",
112:     };
113:     setTickets((prev) => [ticket, ...prev]);
114:     return ticket;
115:   }, []);
116: 
117:   const resetMockData = useCallback(() => {
118:     setTickets([]);
119:     setInventory(createInitialInventory());
120:   }, []);
121: 
122:   const getTicket = useCallback((id: string) => tickets.find((ticket) => ticket.id === id), [tickets]);
123: 
124:   const value = useMemo(
125:     () => ({ tickets, inventory, simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket }),
126:     [tickets, inventory, simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket],
127:   );
128: 
129:   return <SwapDeskContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</SwapDeskContext.Provider>;
130: }
131: 
132: export function useSwapDesk() {
133:   const context = useContext(SwapDeskContext);
134:   if (!context) {
135:     throw new Error("useSwapDesk must be used within a SwapDeskProvider");
136:   }
137:   return context;
138: }

2: title: Proxy
3: nav_title: Proxy
4: description: Use Next.js Proxy to rewrite, redirect, modify headers, or respond directly before a request completes.
5: related:
6:   title: API Reference
7:   description: Learn more about Proxy
8:   links:
9:     - app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy
10:     - app/guides/backend-for-frontend
11: ---
12: 
13: ## Proxy
14: 
15: > **Good to know**: Starting with Next.js 16, Middleware is now called Proxy to better reflect its purpose. The functionality remains the same.
16: 
17: Proxy allows you to run code before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.
18: 
19: ### Use cases
20: 
21: Some common scenarios where Proxy is effective include:
22: 
23: - Modifying headers for all pages or a subset of pages
24: - Rewriting to different pages based on A/B tests or experiments
25: - Programmatic redirects based on incoming request properties
26: 
27: For simple redirects, consider using the [`redirects`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/redirects) configuration in `next.config.ts` first. Proxy should be used when you need access to request data or more complex logic.
28: 
29: Proxy is _not_ intended for slow data fetching. While Proxy can be helpful for [optimistic checks](/docs/app/guides/authentication#optimistic-checks-with-proxy-optional) such as permission-based redirects, it should not be used as a full session management or authorization solution.
30: 
31: Using fetch with `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, or `options.next.tags`, has no effect in Proxy.
32: 
33: ### Convention
34: 
35: Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.
36: 
37: > **Note**: While only one `proxy.ts` file is supported per project, you can still organize your proxy logic into modules. Break out proxy functionalities into separate `.ts` or `.js` files and import them into your main `proxy.ts` file. This allows for cleaner management of route-specific proxy, aggregated in the `proxy.ts` for centralized control. By enforcing a single proxy file, it simplifies configuration, prevents potential conflicts, and optimizes performance by avoiding multiple proxy layers.
38: 
39: ### Example
40: 
41: You can export your proxy function as either a default export or a named `proxy` export:
42: 
43: ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
44: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
45: import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
46: 
47: // This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
48: export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
49:   return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
50: }
51: 
52: // Alternatively, you can use a default export:
53: // export default function proxy(request: NextRequest) { ... }
54: 
55: export const config = {
56:   matcher: '/about/:path*',
57: }
58: ```
59: 
60: ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
61: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
62: 
63: // This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
64: export function proxy(request) {
65:   return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
66: }
67: 
68: // Alternatively, you can use a default export:
69: // export default function proxy(request) { ... }
70: 
71: export const config = {
72:   matcher: '/about/:path*',
73: }
74: ```
75: 
76: The `matcher` config allows you to filter Proxy to run on specific paths. See the [Matcher](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#matcher) documentation for more details on path matching.
77: 
78: Read more about [using `proxy`](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#proxy), or refer to the `proxy` [API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

## Demo Flow

The store reads live data from the SwapDesk API and keeps a local demo fallback when the backend is offline.

1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`).
2. Pick a handling mode: **Deterministic** (`POST /v1/tickets`) or **Agent** (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`).
3. In Deterministic mode, choose a fixture order/item (from `GET /v1/fixtures`) and a requested size, then submit.
4. The case is created by the backend; its status, outcome, and reply appear instantly in **Mission Control**, filterable by status, and persist across reloads.
5. Open a case to inspect its live execution timeline (`GET .../timeline`) and, for clarification/escalation outcomes, continue it with a consent size (`POST .../continue`).
6. **Settings → Demo Fault Injection** arms/clears demo faults (`POST`/`DELETE /v1/demo/faults`).
7. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears the local queue and restores demo defaults.

## State Management

`src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:

```ts
const {
  tickets, inventory, fixtures, health, apiError,
  refreshHealth, loadFixtures,
  submitTicket, submitAgentTicket, getCase, getTimeline, continueCase,
  armFault, clearFaults,
  simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket,
} = useSwapDesk();
```

- `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"` (arranged → resolved, clarification → processing, denial/escalation → escalated).
- `submitTicket(input)` / `submitAgentTicket(input)` — create a case through the API and prepend it to the queue.
- `getCase(id)` / `getTimeline(id)` / `continueCase(id, input)` — live status, timeline, and continuation for a case.
- `health` — `"unknown" | "online" | "offline"` from `GET /v1/health`; surfaced in the top bar.
- `simulateTicket()` / `submitCustomerTicket()` — offline demo helpers kept as a fallback.
- `resetMockData()` / `getTicket(id)` — local queue reset and lookup.

14: ## Startup
15: 
16: ```bash
17: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
18: uv run python -m swapdesk.worker
19: ```
20: 
21: API and worker share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`). Agent
22: checkpoints live at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`. knobs:
23: 
24: | Variable | Default | Purpose |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | `SWAPDESK_WORKER_POLL_MS` | `200` | Queue poll interval |
27: | `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` | `12` | Max provider requests per run (hard cap, not a recursion limit) |
28: | `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` | `300` | Wall-clock execution timeout per run |
29: | `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS` | unset (disabled) | Set `1` for explicit local fault testing |
30: | `SWAPDESK_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000` | Allowed frontend origins |

32: ## Concepts
33: 
34: - `execution_status`: queue/worker state — `queued | running |
35:   waiting_input | completed | failed`.
36: - `outcome`: business result — `arranged | clarification | denial |
37:   escalation | null` (`null` until a run completes).
38: - `clarification` parks the case in `waiting_input`; continue through the
39:   same agent path with message/consent.
40: - Terminal outcomes (`arranged`, `denial`, `escalation`) return their
41:   saved result with no further model call.
42: - `trace_id` is the local checkpoint thread (`case_id:run_id`); `null`
43:   when no run completed. Never a URL, never invented.
44: - Timeline holds journal/operation events only (ids, sizes, policy
45:   phrases). Agent reasoning and credentials are never exposed.
46: - Failed or timed-out runs are never retried automatically; an explicit
47:   continue queues a fresh run. Cancellation limits: an in-flight model
48:   call cannot be cancelled, so a timed-out attempt may still commit late;
49:   operation keys are idempotent, so late commits cannot double-apply.

51: ## POST /v1/agent/tickets → 202
52: 
53: Request:
54: 
55: ```json
56: {
57:   "message": "My Jordan 4s are too tight, need size 43",
58:   "order_id": "ORD-1001",
59:   "order_item_id": "ITEM-01",
60:   "size": "43",
61:   "qty": 1,
62:   "consent_size": null,
63:   "case_id": null,
64:   "idempotency_key": "storefront-abc-123"
65: }
66: ```
67: 
68: - `message` is required and non-blank. `order_id` / `order_item_id` /
69:   `size` may be missing: the agent asks for information instead.
70: - Supplied fields travel as structured request data; `consent_size` is
71:   recorded only when explicitly supplied, never fabricated.
72: - Idempotency: effective key = `idempotency_key` or `case_id`. Same key
73:   + same payload returns the existing case (`duplicate: true`, no new
74:   run). Same key + different payload is `409`.

1: """Durable work queue for the customer agent path. One concern only.
2: 
3: POST /v1/agent/tickets persists the accepted request here and returns
4: 202; a single worker claims queued runs atomically and executes them
5: through service.submit_agent_ticket (the one agent execution
6: implementation). Status/timeline reads never block on the worker: short
7: connections, WAL, IMMEDIATE only on writes.
8: 
9: Interrupted `running` rows are marked `failed` on worker startup and are
10: never replayed blindly; an explicit continue starts a fresh RUN-n with
11: preserved consent and fresh action keys. Paid executions are never
12: retried automatically.
13: """
14:

16:

29:   idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
30:   case_id TEXT NOT NULL,
31:   payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
32:   payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,

137:     if not isinstance(qty, int) or qty < 1:
138:         raise ValueError("qty must be at least 1")
139:     case_id = _check_id(case_id, "case_id")
140:     idempotency_key = _check_id(idempotency_key, "idempotency_key")
141:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
142:     payload = _canonical_request(
143:         message=message.strip(), order_id=order_id,
144:         order_item_id=order_item_id, size=size, qty=qty,
145:         consent_size=consent_size)
146:     digest = payload_hash(payload)
147:     key = idempotency_key or case_id
148: 
149:     conn = connect(db_path)
150:     try:
151:         with _db.immediate(conn):
152:             if key is not None:
153:                 saved = conn.execute(
154:                     "SELECT * FROM submissions WHERE idempotency_key = ?",
155:                     (key,)).fetchone()
156:                 if saved is not None:
157:                     if saved["payload_hash"] != digest:
158:                         raise SubmissionConflict(
159:                             f"submission key {key!r} was already used "
160:                             "with a different payload")
161:                     existing = saved["case_id"]
162:                     first = conn.execute(
163:                         "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
164:                         "ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1", (existing,)).fetchone()
165:                     return {"case_id": existing,
166:                             "run_id": first["run_id"] if first else "RUN-1",
167:                             "execution_status": _case_execution(conn,
168:                                                                existing),
169:                             "duplicate": True}
170:             cid = case_id or _new_case_id()
171:             existing_runs = [r["run_id"] for r in conn.execute(
172:                 "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ?", (cid,))]
173:             if existing_runs:
174:                 # Explicit case_id reuse never starts a new exchange.
175:                 first = conn.execute(
176:                     "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
177:                     "ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1", (cid,)).fetchone()
178:                 if key is not None:
179:                     conn.execute(
180:                         "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO submissions "
181:                         "(idempotency_key, case_id, payload_hash, "
182:                         "payload_json, created_at) "
183:                         "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
184:                         (key, cid, digest,
185:                          json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), _db.utcnow()))
186:                 return {"case_id": cid, "run_id": first["run_id"],
187:                         "execution_status": _case_execution(conn, cid),
188:                         "duplicate": True}
189:             run_id = "RUN-1"
190:             now = _db.utcnow()
191:             conn.execute(
192:                 "INSERT INTO runs (case_id, run_id, thread_id, state, "
193:                 "request_json, created_at, updated_at) "
194:                 "VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'queued', ?, ?, ?)",
195:                 (cid, run_id, _new_thread_id(cid, run_id),
196:                  json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), now, now))
197:             if key is not None:
198:                 conn.execute(
199:                     "INSERT INTO submissions (idempotency_key, case_id, "
200:                     "payload_hash, payload_json, created_at) "
201:                     "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
202:                     (key, cid, digest,
203:                      json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), now))
204:             return {"case_id": cid, "run_id": run_id,
205:                     "execution_status": "queued", "duplicate": False}
206:     finally:
207:         conn.close()
208: 
209: 
210: def _case_execution(conn, case_id: str) -> str:
211:     rows = conn.execute(
212:         "SELECT run_id, state, outcome FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
213:         "ORDER BY rowid", (case_id,)).fetchall()
214:     if not rows:
215:         return "queued"
216:     states = [r["state"] for r in rows]
217:     if "running" in states:
218:         return "running"
219:     if "queued" in states:
220:         return "queued"
221:     last = rows[-1]
222:     if last["state"] == "failed":
223:         return "failed"
224:     if last["outcome"] == "clarification":
225:         return "waiting_input"
226:     return "completed"
227: 
228: 
229: def _latest_request(conn, case_id: str) -> dict:
230:     row = conn.execute(
231:         "SELECT request_json FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY rowid DESC "
232:         "LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
233:     return json.loads(row["request_json"]) if row else {}
234: 
235: 
236: def continue_agent_request(db_path, case_id: str, *, message: str = "",
237:                            consent_size: str | None = None,
238:                            order_id: str | None = None,
239:                            order_item_id: str | None = None,
240:                            size: str | None = None,
241:                            qty: int = 1) -> dict | None:
242:     """Queue a continuation run through the same agent path.
243: 
244:     Returns None when the case is unknown to the queue. Terminal cases
245:     return their saved result with continued=False and no model call.
246:     """
247:     from . import service as _service
248: 
249:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
250:     conn = connect(db_path)
251:     try:
252:         with _db.immediate(conn):
253:             runs = conn.execute(
254:                 "SELECT run_id, state, outcome FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
255:                 "ORDER BY rowid", (case_id,)).fetchall()
256:             if not runs:
257:                 return None
258:             states = [r["state"] for r in runs]
259:             if "running" in states or "queued" in states:
260:                 raise ConcurrentRun(
261:                     f"case {case_id!r} already has a queued or running run")
262:             if runs[-1]["state"] == "completed" \
263:                     and runs[-1]["outcome"] in TERMINAL_OUTCOMES:
264:                 current = _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id)
265:                 return {**current, "continued": False}
266:             has_input = bool((message or "").strip()) \
267:                 or consent_size is not None \
268:                 or order_id is not None or order_item_id is not None \
269:                 or size is not None
270:             if not has_input:
271:                 raise ValueError(
272:                     "continue requires a message, consent_size, or "
273:                     "explicit order fields")
274:             if not isinstance(qty, int) or qty < 1:
275:                 raise ValueError("qty must be at least 1")
276:             base = _latest_request(conn, case_id)
277:             effective = {
278:                 "message": message.strip() or base.get("message", ""),
279:                 "order_id": order_id if order_id is not None
280:                 else base.get("order_id"),
281:                 "order_item_id": order_item_id if order_item_id is not None
282:                 else base.get("order_item_id"),
283:                 "size": size if size is not None else base.get("size"),
284:                 "qty": qty,
285:                 # Preserve recorded consent; explicit consent overrides.
286:                 "consent_size": consent_size if consent_size is not None
287:                 else base.get("consent_size"),
288:             }
289:             if not effective["message"]:
290:                 raise ValueError("message must not be blank")
291:             run_id = _next_run_id([r["run_id"] for r in runs])
292:             now = _db.utcnow()
293:             conn.execute(
294:                 "INSERT INTO runs (case_id, run_id, thread_id, state, "
295:                 "request_json, created_at, updated_at) "
296:                 "VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'queued', ?, ?, ?)",
297:                 (case_id, run_id, _new_thread_id(case_id, run_id),
298:                  json.dumps(effective, sort_keys=True), now, now))
299:             return {"case_id": case_id, "run_id": run_id,
300:                     "execution_status": "queued", "continued": True,
301:                     "outcome": None, "reply": None, "exchange_id": None}
302:     finally:
303:         conn.close()
304: 
305: 
306: def claim_next_run(db_path, worker_id: str = "worker-1") -> dict | None:
307:     """Atomically claim the oldest queued run whose case is idle."""
308:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
309:     conn = connect(db_path)
310:     try:
311:         with _db.immediate(conn):
312:             row = conn.execute(
313:                 "SELECT case_id, run_id, thread_id, request_json FROM runs "
314:                 "WHERE state = 'queued' "
315:                 "AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs r2 "
316:                 "WHERE r2.case_id = runs.case_id AND r2.state = 'running') "
317:                 "ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1").fetchone()
318:             if row is None:
319:                 return None
320:             updated = conn.execute(
321:                 "UPDATE runs SET state = 'running', updated_at = ? "
322:                 "WHERE case_id = ? AND run_id = ? AND state = 'queued'",
323:                 (_db.utcnow(), row["case_id"], row["run_id"]))
324:             assert updated.rowcount == 1
325:             _ = worker_id
326:             return {"case_id": row["case_id"], "run_id": row["run_id"],
327:                     "thread_id": row["thread_id"],
328:                     "request": json.loads(row["request_json"])}
329:     finally:
330:         conn.close()
331: 
332: 
333: def finish_run(db_path, *, case_id: str, run_id: str, outcome: str | None,
334:                reply: str | None, exchange_id: str | None,
335:                error: str | None, trace_id: str | None,
336:                requests_spent: int | None = None) -> None:
337:     """Record a run's terminal state. requests_spent is the client-side
338:     count of model generations consumed (ground truth independent of
339:     telemetry capture)."""
340:     state = "completed" if error is None else "failed"
341:     conn = connect(db_path)
342:     try:
343:         with _db.immediate(conn):
344:             conn.execute(
345:                 "UPDATE runs SET state = ?, outcome = ?, reply = ?, "
346:                 "exchange_id = ?, error = ?, trace_id = ?, "
347:                 "requests_spent = ?, updated_at = ? "
348:                 "WHERE case_id = ? AND run_id = ?",
349:                 (state, outcome, reply, exchange_id, error, trace_id,
350:                  requests_spent, _db.utcnow(), case_id, run_id))
351:     finally:
352:         conn.close()
353: 
354: 
355: def mark_interrupted_failed(db_path, reason: str) -> int:
356:     """Mark leftover running rows failed. Never requeues. Returns count."""
357:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
358:     conn = connect(db_path)
359:     try:
360:         with _db.immediate(conn):
361:             cur = conn.execute(
362:                 "UPDATE runs SET state = 'failed', error = ?, "
363:                 "updated_at = ? WHERE state = 'running'",
364:                 (reason, _db.utcnow()))
365:             return cur.rowcount
366:     finally:
367:         conn.close()
368: 
369: 
370: def _cleanup_state(db_path, exchange_id: str | None) -> str | None:
371:     if not exchange_id:
372:         return None
373:     from .operations import verify_exchange
374: 
375:     try:
376:         hand = verify_exchange(db_path, exchange_id)
377:     except Exception:
378:         return None
379:     if hand.pending_cleanup:
380:         return "pending"
381:     if hand.hold_active:
382:         return "held"
383:     return "none"
384: 
385: 
386: def _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id: str) -> dict:
387:     from . import service as _service
388: 
389:     run_rows = conn.execute(
390:         "SELECT run_id, state, outcome, reply, exchange_id, error, trace_id, "
391:         "requests_spent FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY rowid",
392:         (case_id,)).fetchall()
393:     execution = _case_execution(conn, case_id)
394:     last = run_rows[-1]
395:     business = _service.case_status(db_path, case_id)
396:     if business is not None:
397:         outcome: str | None = business["outcome"]
398:         reply: str | None = business["reply"]
399:         exchange_id: str | None = business["exchange_id"]
400:         runs = business["runs"]
401:     else:
402:         outcome, reply, exchange_id = None, None, None
403:         runs = [r["run_id"] for r in run_rows]
404:     clarification = reply if outcome == "clarification" else None
405:     return {
406:         "case_id": case_id,
407:         "execution_status": execution,
408:         "outcome": outcome,
409:         "reply": reply,
410:         "exchange_id": exchange_id,
411:         "runs": sorted(set(runs) | {r["run_id"] for r in run_rows}),
412:         "current_run_id": last["run_id"],
413:         "clarification": clarification,
414:         "cleanup": _cleanup_state(db_path, exchange_id),
415:         "trace_id": last["trace_id"] if last["trace_id"] else None,
416:         "error": last["error"] if last["state"] == "failed" else None,
417:         "requests_spent": last["requests_spent"],
418:     }
419: 
420: 
421: def get_agent_status(db_path, case_id: str) -> dict | None:
422:     """Responsive read-only agent status. None when unknown to the queue."""
423:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
424:     conn = connect(db_path)
425:     try:
426:         known = conn.execute(
427:             "SELECT 1 FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? LIMIT 1",
428:             (case_id,)).fetchone()
429:         if known is None:
430:             return None
431:         return _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id)
432:     finally:
433:         conn.close()
434: 
435: 
436: def get_agent_timeline(db_path, case_id: str) -> list[dict] | None:
437:     """Sanitized journal/operations timeline with run ids. None if unknown."""
438:     from . import service as _service
439: 
440:     ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
441:     conn = connect(db_path)
442:     try:
443:         known = conn.execute(
444:             "SELECT 1 FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? LIMIT 1",
445:             (case_id,)).fetchone()
446:     finally:
447:         conn.close()
448:     if known is None:
449:         return None
450:     events = _service.case_timeline(db_path, case_id)
451:     if events is None:
452:         return []
453:     conn = connect(db_path)
454:     try:
455:         run_of = {r["idempotency_key"]: r["run_id"] for r in conn.execute(
456:             "SELECT idempotency_key, run_id FROM operations "
457:             "WHERE case_id = ?", (case_id,))}
458:     finally:
459:         conn.close()
460:     return [{**event, "run_id": run_of.get(event["op_key"])}
461:             for event in events]

## Objective
- Wire SwapDesk's backend API into the Next.js frontend, implemented endpoint-by-endpoint. Current focus: correct the integration to use the new async `/v1/agent/*` routes mandated by `docs/API_CONTRACT.md` (the earlier wiring used legacy routes).

## Important Details
- **Contract doc `docs/API_CONTRACT.md` is normative for `/v1/agent/*`.** Change notice: `POST /v1/agent/tickets` no longer runs inline (previously 201 + completed outcome); it now persists and returns **202 accepted** with `case_id`, `run_id`, `execution_status`, `status_url` — must poll the status URL.
- **Frontend MUST NOT use legacy routes:** `POST /v1/tickets`, `GET /v1/cases/{id}`, `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`, `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`, `POST/DELETE /v1/demo/faults` (403 unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`). `GET /v1/health` and `GET /v1/fixtures` are unchanged and safe.
- Contract concepts: `execution_status` = `queued | running | waiting_input | completed | failed`; `outcome` = `arranged | clarification | denial | escalation | null`; `clarification` parks in `waiting_input` and is continued via the same agent path.
- Startup: `uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000` + `uv run python -m swapdesk.worker` (API and worker share `SWAPDESK_DB`, default `swapdesk.db`; checkpoints at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`).
- Knobs: `SWAPDESK_WORKER_POLL_MS`=200, `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET`=12, `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S`=300, `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS`=unset, `SWAPDESK_CORS_ORIGINS`=`http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
- Backend now supports CORS (so direct browser calls are possible), but the Next same-origin rewrite proxy still works (target overridable via `SWAPDESK_API_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`).
- Backend models in `src/swapdesk/api.py`: `AgentTicketIn` (message≥1, order_id, order_item_id, size, qty, consent_size, case_id, idempotency_key, resume), `AgentAccepted` (case_id, run_id, execution_status, status_url, duplicate), `AgentStatusOut` (case_id, execution_status, outcome, reply, exchange_id, runs, current_run_id, clarification, …).
- Frontend stack: Next.js 16.4.0 (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents`+`partialPrefetching`), React 19, TS strict, alias `@/*` → `./src/*`, Tailwind v4. `@tanstack/react-query` is a dep but unused.
- Strict ESLint rule `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`; mount-time setState must be wrapped, e.g. `window.setTimeout(() => { ... }, 0)`.
- 3 pre-existing lint errors remain only in untouched files: `frontend/src/components/ui/carousel.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx`, `frontend/src/hook/use-mobile.tsx`.
- Git: pulled commits added backend async queue; `stash@{0}` ("endpoint implementation") applied cleanly (README auto-merged, no conflict markers), all 12 files staged, stash dropped. Nothing pushed. `frontend/package-lock.json` shows 144 deletions (only `"libc": ["glibc"]` churn) — flag, may want `git restore --staged frontend/package-lock.json`.
- Running locally: backend on `:8000`, frontend dev server already on `:3000` (node process on `SwapDesk-1\frontend`). Earlier verified GET/POST proxy through `:3000`.
- `.entire/settings.local.json` created with `"commit_linking": "always"`; test commit `0e1d3b6` has `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. File is gitignored by `.entire/.gitignore`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (typed client) and added same-origin `/v1/:path*` rewrite proxy in `frontend/next.config.ts`.
- Rebuilt `frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx` as API-backed store with offline mock fallback (health, fixtures, submit, case/timeline/continue, faults, localStorage rehydration of live cases).
- Wired legacy endpoints: `GET /v1/health` (AppShell badge + Mission Control pill), `GET /v1/fixtures` (Inventory page), `POST /v1/tickets` + `POST /v1/agent/tickets` (Customer Simulation mode toggle), `GET /v1/cases/{id}` + `/timeline` + `POST .../continue` (ticket detail), `POST`/`DELETE /v1/demo/faults` (Settings panel).
- Updated `README.md` and `frontend/README.md` to document the integration.
- Verified: `npm run build` passes; ESLint clean on changed files (only 3 pre-existing errors); dev routes `/`, `/simulate`, `/inventory`, `/settings`, `/ticket/CASE-ca1a8e50`, `/inbox` return 200; proxy GET/POST confirmed.

### Active
- Migrating frontend off legacy routes onto async `/v1/agent/*` per contract. Just read `src/swapdesk/api.py` lines 40–200 (models); route handlers not yet fully read.

### Blocked
- (none) Potential: Agent mode needs provider config (`.env`); without it the backend returns 503. Demo faults are now 403 unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`.

## Next Move
1. Read `src/swapdesk/api.py` agent route handlers (approx. lines 230–400) to capture exact request/response shapes and status/continue semantics.
2. Update `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (`/v1/agent/tickets` 202 + poll `status_url`, `/v1/agent/cases/{id}`, `/v1/agent/cases/{id}/timeline`, `/v1/agent/cases/{id}/continue`), then adjust `store/swapdesk.tsx` + UI (poll `execution_status`, handle `waiting_input`), and gate/relabel the demo faults panel.

## Relevant Files
- `docs/API_CONTRACT.md`: normative agent-path contract and change notice.
- `src/swapdesk/api.py`: route/model definitions (agent + legacy); source of truth.
- `src/swapdesk/queue.py`, `src/swapdesk/worker.py`: newly pulled async queue implementation.
- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`: typed client to migrate to `/v1/agent/*`.
- `frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`: API-backed store; needs polling + agent actions.
- `frontend/next.config.ts`: `/v1/:path*` rewrite proxy (`SWAPDESK_API_URL`).
- `frontend/src/components/CustomerSimulationWidget.tsx`: mode toggle → agent vs deterministic.
- `frontend/src/components/AppShell.tsx`: health badge.
- `frontend/app/inventory/page.tsx`: fixtures catalogue + policy.
- `frontend/app/settings/page.tsx`: demo fault panel (POST/DELETE `/v1/demo/faults`).
- `frontend/app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`: case status/timeline/continue UI.
- `frontend/app/mission-control.tsx`: health pill + ticket queue.
- `README.md`, `frontend/README.md`: updated integration docs.
- `frontend/package-lock.json`: staged churn (144 `libc` deletions) — decide whether to unstage.
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.

20:     this.name = "ApiError";
21:     this.status = status;

26: async function request<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {

28:   try {

30:       ...init,

1: # SwapDesk Frontend
2: 
3: The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.
4: 
5: Built as a Next.js app that talks to the **SwapDesk FastAPI backend** for live data. When the backend is unreachable it falls back to built-in client-side demo state, so the dashboard still runs standalone.
6: 
7: ## Tech Stack
8: 
9: - **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
10: - **React 19** with Server & Client Components
11: - **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
12: - **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
13: - **lucide-react** icons
14: - **sonner** toasts
15: - Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)
16: 
17: ## Getting Started
18: 
19: ```bash
20: npm install      # install dependencies
21: npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
22: ```
23: 
24: Other scripts:
25: 
26: | Script          | Description                                    |
27: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
28: | `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
29: | `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
30: | `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |
31: 
32: ## Environment Variables
33: 
34: | Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
35: | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |
37: | `SWAPDESK_API_URL`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8000`             | Server-side proxy target for `/v1/*` requests (configured in `next.config.ts`). |
38: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SWAPDESK_API_URL` | _(unset)_                     | Set to call the API cross-origin from the browser directly instead of through the proxy. That origin must allow CORS. |
39: 
40: The browser calls same-origin `/v1/*` paths and Next.js rewrites them to `SWAPDESK_API_URL`, so no CORS setup is needed for local development. Start the backend first:
41: 
42: ```bash
43: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app   # from the repository root
44: ```
45: 
46: ## Backend API integration
47: 
48: `src/lib/api.ts` is the typed client; `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` calls it and exposes the results to the UI.
49: 
50: | Endpoint                        | Used by                                                            |
51: | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
52: | `GET /v1/health`                | `AppShell` + Mission Control connection badge                      |
53: | `GET /v1/fixtures`              | Inventory page (fixture catalogue + return policy) and pickers     |
54: | `POST /v1/tickets`              | Customer Simulation — Deterministic mode                           |
55: | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`        | Customer Simulation — Agent mode                                   |
56: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`            | Ticket detail outcome summary                                      |
57: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`   | Ticket detail execution timeline                                   |
58: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`  | Ticket detail "Continue case" (clarification consent)              |
59: | `POST /v1/demo/faults`          | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (arm a failure)                    |
60: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`        | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (clear all failures)               |

98: ## Demo Flow
99: 
100: The store reads live data from the SwapDesk API and keeps a local demo fallback when the backend is offline.
101: 
102: 1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`).
103: 2. Pick a handling mode: **Deterministic** (`POST /v1/tickets`) or **Agent** (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`).
104: 3. In Deterministic mode, choose a fixture order/item (from `GET /v1/fixtures`) and a requested size, then submit.
105: 4. The case is created by the backend; its status, outcome, and reply appear instantly in **Mission Control**, filterable by status, and persist across reloads.
106: 5. Open a case to inspect its live execution timeline (`GET .../timeline`) and, for clarification/escalation outcomes, continue it with a consent size (`POST .../continue`).
107: 6. **Settings → Demo Fault Injection** arms/clears demo faults (`POST`/`DELETE /v1/demo/faults`).
108: 7. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears the local queue and restores demo defaults.
109: 
110: ## State Management
111: 
112: `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:
113: 
114: ```ts
115: const {
116:   tickets, inventory, fixtures, health, apiError,
117:   refreshHealth, loadFixtures,
118:   submitTicket, submitAgentTicket, getCase, getTimeline, continueCase,
119:   armFault, clearFaults,
120:   simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket,
121: } = useSwapDesk();
122: ```
123: 
124: - `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"` (arranged → resolved, clarification → processing, denial/escalation → escalated).
125: - `submitTicket(input)` / `submitAgentTicket(input)` — create a case through the API and prepend it to the queue.
126: - `getCase(id)` / `getTimeline(id)` / `continueCase(id, input)` — live status, timeline, and continuation for a case.
127: - `health` — `"unknown" | "online" | "offline"` from `GET /v1/health`; surfaced in the top bar.
128: - `simulateTicket()` / `submitCustomerTicket()` — offline demo helpers kept as a fallback.
129: - `resetMockData()` / `getTicket(id)` — local queue reset and lookup.
130: 
131: ## Routes
132: 
133: | Route                 | Page                    | Type            | Notes                              |
134: | --------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
135: | `/`                   | Mission Control         | server + client | metrics + live queue, filter       |
136: | `/inbox`              | Inbox                   | server          | static ticket list                 |
137: | `/inventory`          | Inventory               | server layout + client page | stock reacts to simulations |
138: | `/database`           | Database Schema         | server          |                                    |
139: | `/integrations`       | Integrations            | server layout + client page | webhook toggle + URL copy  |
140: | `/settings`           | Agent Settings          | server          |                                    |
141: | `/simulate`           | Customer Simulation     | server          | `CustomerSimulationWidget`         |
142: | `/ticket/[id]`        | Ticket Execution        | client          | Partial Prerender (Suspense)       |
143: | `/robots.txt`         | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
144: | `/sitemap.xml`        | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
145: | `/opengraph-image`    | —                       | image route     | generated 1200×630 PNG             |
146: | `/twitter-image`      | —                       | image route     | re-export of opengraph-image       |
147: 
148: > **Turbopack dynamic route note:** `/ticket/[id]` must pre-render its HTML shell at build time. Client hooks that need URL data (`useParams`, `usePathname`) therefore live behind `<Suspense>` and out of the static shell. See `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`.
149: 
150: ## Design System
151: 
152: Theme tokens live in `app/globals.css` as CSS variables and Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings:
153: 
154: - Colors: `--card: #111113`, `--border: #222225`, `--color-success` (green), `--color-primary`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`, `--color-hairline`
155: - Type: `font-display` (`--font-bricolage`), `font-sans` (`--font-jakarta`), `font-mono` (`--font-geist-mono`)
156: - Utilities: `panel` (card), `glass` (frosted nav), `pulse-dot`, `num` (tabular numerals), `rise` (entry animation)
157: 
158: > **Guideline:** keep server-rendered pages static where possible and move interactivity into client components. Do not introduce a visual redesign — extend the existing token system.
159: 
160: ## SEO
161: 
162: Add full metadata to every segment:
163: 
164: - Root (`app/layout.tsx`): `metadataBase`, titles with `template: "%s · SwapDesk"`, description, keywords, `<viewport>` (themeColor), OpenGraph + Twitter cards, `robots`, `applicationName`, authors, category.
165: - Per page: use the `pageMetadata({ title, description, path })` helper from `src/lib/seo.ts` (marked `Export const metadata`).
166: - Images: `app/opengraph-image.tsx` generates a themed 1200×630 card with `ImageResponse`; `app/twitter-image.tsx` re-exports it.

1: # SwapDesk
2: 
3: SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.
4: 
5: All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.
6: 
7: ## Repository layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: frontend/          Next.js dashboard — live API integration, local demo fallback
11: src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
12: eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
13: tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
14: docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
15: hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
16: ```
17: 
18: ## The two halves
19: 
20: - **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
21: - **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It calls the live backend API through a same-origin proxy (`/v1/*` → FastAPI, configured in `frontend/next.config.ts`) and falls back to built-in demo state when the backend is unreachable. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## Backend
26: 
27: ### Features
28: 
29: - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
30: - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
31: - Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
32: - One active exchange per order item, across cases.
33: - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
34: - Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
35: - Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
36: - A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
37: - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).
38: 
39: ### Installation
40: 
41: Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
42: 
43: ```bash
44: git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
45: cd SwapDesk
46: uv sync
47: ```
48: 
49: ### Test
50: 
51: ```bash
52: uv run pytest -q
53: ```
54: 
55: The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.
56: 
57: ### Run the API and worker
58: 
59: ```bash
60: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
61: uv run python -m swapdesk.worker
62: ```
63: 
64: Both share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`); agent checkpoints live
65: at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`. Interactive docs at
66: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always
67: in sync). Normative customer contract:
68: [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md).
69: 
70: | Method & route                         | What it does                                              |
71: | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
72: | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`               | Accept an agent ticket, queue RUN-1, return 202 + status URL |
73: | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}`             | Execution status + verified outcome when available (404 unknown) |
74: | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}/timeline`    | Sanitized action/journal events with run ids (404 unknown) |
75: | `POST /v1/agent/cases/{id}/continue`   | Queue a continuation run, or report terminal unchanged (404/409/422) |
76: | `POST /v1/tickets`                     | Legacy deterministic demo path (201, benchmark use; frontend must not use it) |
77: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`                   | Legacy deterministic status (frontend must not use it)    |
78: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`          | Legacy deterministic timeline (frontend must not use it)  |
79: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`         | Legacy deterministic continuation (frontend must not use it) |
80: | `GET /v1/fixtures`                     | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns         |
81: | `POST /v1/demo/faults`                 | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
82: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`               | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
83: | `GET /v1/health`                       | Liveness probe                                            |
84: 
85: `POST /v1/agent/tickets` returns **202 accepted** with `case_id`,
86: `run_id`, `execution_status`, and `status_url` — never a completed
87: outcome. `execution_status` (`queued`/`running`/`waiting_input`/
88: `completed`/`failed`) is distinct from the business `outcome`
89: (`arranged`/`clarification`/`denial`/`escalation`, null until a run
90: completes). Malformed requests return 422, unknown cases 404,
91: submission conflicts or concurrent runs 409, disabled demo controls
92: 403. A run is bounded by `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` provider requests and
93: `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock seconds; failed runs are never
94: retried automatically.
95: 
96: `POST /v1/tickets` remains the legacy deterministic demo path used by
97: benchmarks. The customer frontend must use `/v1/agent/*`. The agent
98: route accepts optional structured order fields as request data; the
99: customer message remains the primary input, and consent is recorded
100: only when explicitly supplied.
101: 
102: ```bash
103: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/tickets \
104:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
105:   -d '{"message":"Exchange item ITEM-01 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
106: 
107: curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx
108: curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
109: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
110:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
111:   -d '{"message":"42 is fine","consent_size":"42"}'
112: ```
113: 
114: No authentication: this is a local mock. Agent status and timeline
115: reads are read-only and never block on the worker.
116: 
117: ### Configuring the agent
118: 
119: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):
120: 
121: - `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
122: - `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
123: - `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
124: - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.
125: 
126: Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.
127: 
128: ### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio
129: 
130: Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: uv run langgraph dev
134: ```
135: 
136: Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:
137: 
138: - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
139: - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.
140: 
141: Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
142: 
143: ## Frontend
144: 
145: A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.
146: 
147: ### Run it
148: 
149: ```bash
150: cd frontend
151: npm install
152: npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
153: ```
154: 
155: Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.
156: 
157: ### Pages and demo flow
158: 
159: | Route           | Page                | What it demos                                        |
160: | --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
161: | `/`             | Mission Control     | Agent metrics + live execution queue                 |
162: | `/inbox`        | Inbox               | Sample ticket stream                                 |
163: | `/inventory`    | Inventory           | Stock levels that react to simulations               |
164: | `/database`     | Database Schema     | Tables the agent reads/writes                        |
165: | `/integrations` | Integrations        | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
166: | `/settings`     | Agent Settings      | Autonomy/guardrail config UI                         |
167: | `/simulate`     | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue           |
168: | `/ticket/[id]`  | Ticket Execution    | Per-ticket action timeline                           |
169: 
170: The dashboard calls the backend through a same-origin proxy (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` + a `next.config.ts` rewrite), and falls back to a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`) when the backend is offline. **Customer Simulation** runs a case in Deterministic (`POST /v1/tickets`) or Agent (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`) mode; **Inventory** renders the `GET /v1/fixtures` catalogue; **ticket detail** reads `GET /v1/cases/{id}` and its timeline; **Settings** arms/clears demo faults. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the local demo state. Completion rate is computed from the queue and cost shows "Demo Mode".
171: 
172: SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.
173: 
174: ## Evaluation and evidence
175: 
176: - `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
177: - `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
178: - `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
179: - `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
180: - `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.
181: 
182: ## Documentation
183:
